competitive_landscape: Today the only practical Saudi↔Bahrain link is the King Fahd Causeway; passenger ferries have been intermittent at best. The congestion itself is the demand signal — there is no premium, on-demand, or clean crossing. Wide-open corridor with acute, quantified pain.

regulatory_note: Cross-border Saudi↔Bahrain service touches Saudi MAWANI/border authorities and Bahraini maritime/immigration; a second fixed causeway (King Hamad Causeway) is also planned, underscoring official recognition of the corridor's strain. PIF/Vision-2030 alignment supports clean-mobility positioning.
seasonality: Gulf summers are extreme heat (climate-controlled cabins, lower energy per mile help); the Shamal winds (winter/spring) bring choppier seas where foiling's smoother ride extends the operable window over conventional craft.

summary: Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province — Dammam, Al Khobar, Dhahran — is the Kingdom's industrial and energy heartland (Saudi Aramco HQ) and its Gulf-facing waterfront. Its defining mobility fact is the King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain: the only land link, now carrying record passenger volumes with hours-long border queues. A direct cross-Gulf foiling crossing from Khobar to Manama (~25 nm) bypasses the causeway entirely — one of the most compelling marine-mobility cases in MENA.
tagline: The Gulf's busiest land border — and an obvious case for a crossing by sea.
